Both fields below are stale, not today's numbers. Don't read them as current.

⚠️ Decisions needed

1. Price feed has been down 27 straight days (Yahoo query1/query2 + stooq all EGRESS_BLOCKED again this morning) — this skill cannot show you a live price on anything until that's fixed.
2. SPXC's status is still unconfirmed. A relayed IBKR snapshot from Sep 29 showed only GOOG open and cash at $432.16, consistent with SPXC having filled its $205 exit-limit (small net profit) rather than the $186.90 stop. Nobody has pulled the actual fill record yet. This has been flagged since Oct 1 and the file is now 42 calendar days past the original 8/25 exit decision.
Action: open IBKR directly, confirm SPXC's fill (or lack of one), and run portfolio-manager to sync positions/cash. Everything below this is built around the current, stale portfolio.json.

Implication: this isn't new information for your sizing — keep positions bracketed, don't lean on "the market will carry it" if a name goes against you.

Last historical episodes at this level: 2000 dot-com peak, 2021 COVID bubble peak.

⏳ Pending Watchlist

💵 Cash deployment

portfolio.json shows $330.60 cash (dated Aug 25). The Sep 29 IBKR relay suggested $432.16 instead (consistent with SPXC having exited at a profit). Deployable is ≥$30 either way, but I'm not recommending a number off either figure — they disagree by $100 and neither is confirmed today. Sync cash via portfolio-manager first. No fresh candidate generated here by design — run stock-finder once cash is confirmed and you want ideas. Your call.

🔄 Rotation suggestions

None generated today. Watchlist has no live candidates (all archived), and I won't suggest trimming/rotating GOOG or SPXC without a confirmed price and confirmed position state — that's exactly the kind of naked suggestion the Aug 5 commission rules exist to prevent. Once IBKR is checked, re-run this to get real numbers.

📚 Today you learned

Working Blind, Part 3 — The Cost of a Month-Long Blackout

Parts 1 and 2 were about triangulating a dead feed day-to-day. Part 3 is about what happens when "day-to-day" becomes 27 days straight: small unknowns compound. One unconfirmed SPXC fill, left alone for a month, turns into a stale cash figure, a stale concentration %, and a stale "what can I deploy" number — none individually dangerous, all now tangled together. The fix was never going to be a better web search; it's closing the loop with the actual source of truth (IBKR) the moment the automated feed fails, not after six weeks of flagging it. In forex you'd never let a position sit unconfirmed this long because your broker statement is always one click away — treat IBKR the same way here. The lesson isn't patience, it's that unreconciled state has a half-life, and letting it ride past that point is itself a decision.

Also today: Data staleness decay — the longer a figure goes unverified, the less a fresh "update" note actually helps, because each one just re-flags the same gap instead of closing it.

Research output, not financial advice. Prices: Yahoo Finance JSON API (query1/query2) and stooq — both EGRESS_BLOCKED at fetch time, 2026-10-06 ~daily-check run (27th consecutive blocked day). No price was estimated or substituted for a live quote; web-search figures mentioned above are explicitly unverified context, not trade-grade data. Verify halal compliance quarterly on Zoya or Musaffa. Generated 2026-10-06 Kuwait time.
